track: D: deterministic ACK provider, 250ms fixed response delay; no real-model quality or cost ranking
cold: first task after a new native service reaches carrier readiness; fresh owned state/workspace/session. Shared npm installation and runner OS file cache retained; not a cold host/cache experiment
warm: new distinct native session after exactly one accepted priming task on the same service. Priming excluded from task-phase deltas and retained in lifecycle totals
equal_work: four distinct fresh native sessions each perform identical ACK operation. Both sequential and concurrent arms use one accepted priming task on a fresh service. All four classified terminal outcomes required; no throughput arrival-rate sweep
provider: record actual task request arrivals/response releases/active count; do not schedule or enforce product concurrency. Session-title auxiliary calls remain separately labeled
task_terminal: exact native assistant ACK of unique submitted marker; initial request must show native session binding and no other fresh-session marker. Native errors retained as outcomes; healthy calibration failure blocks formal admission
resources: dedicated native cgroup 2 CPUs, 3GiB memory/no swap; full lifecycle counters plus active phase CPU deltas, sampled integrated RSS and peak PSS, native process maps and owned disk inventory. Model fixture/controller outside; observer CPU and memory-reader command CPU retained separately. Memory integration estimates from samples, sub-sample peaks may be missed
deadlines: 90s carrier readiness, 60s synthetic HTTP operation, 10s shutdown. Preparation safeguards identify failure, not a universal real-task quota
formal_admission: one complete pilot block (five arms per product), publish measured elapsed time including setup/cleanup before admitting two complete formal blocks; reverse product order in second block
limits: resident service cost separated from active increments
no sustainable capacity, p99, leak or statistical product-ranking claim
